videos.script: Every lesson so far protected the data as it is. This one changes the data, so that less of it is dangerous. {{change}} Support sees a CPF with most of its digits hidden. Developers get a copy with the same shape and nobody in it. The CPF itself leaves the table, replaced by two strings the database cannot turn back into a number. {{cpf}} Then the hard part. An export with no names in it, where almost every customer is still the only one of their kind. Birth date, sex and postcode are enough. {{alone}} Masked, tokenised and pseudonymised data are still personal data. Only anonymous data is not, and anonymous is something you measure, not something you call it. {{measure}} By the end you can say which technique a request needs, and show the number that backs the claim. {{end}}
